name: Morgan & Morgan
dek: A clearer path to legal help for people who fear the cost of asking.

at_a_glance.role: Sole UX/UI designer, end to end
at_a_glance.scope: Competitor analysis, user journey, design system, hi-fi homepage, usability testing
at_a_glance.hard_part: Earning trust from stressed, first-time visitors fast enough that they act before hesitation about cost and outcome wins.
at_a_glance.look_for: How every section answers one objection in sequence: can I trust them, can they win, what will it cost, what do I do now.

problem.claim_h2: The biggest barrier to legal help is asking
problem.thesis: People with a real case often never contact a firm, because cost feels unknowable, outcomes feel uncertain, and the process feels built for lawyers, not for them.
problem.body: Accident victims land on a law firm's homepage in a stressful moment, and most firms answer with dense navigation, vague credentials, and no clear first step. The homepage had to convert hesitation into a single low-risk action: a free case evaluation.
bullets: Upfront cost fears stop people from finding out whether their case is even viable.
Firms rarely show real results, so visitors have no way to judge credibility.
Confusing structure and jargon leave people unsure where the process starts.
problem.research_note: A competitor pass across firms like Cellino & Barnes, Jacoby & Meyers, The Barnes Firm, and Law Tigers showed strong brands undercut by dated design, crowded layouts, and buried consultation paths.

design.claim_h2: One page, four objections, one action
design.intro: The homepage is sequenced as an argument: establish credibility, prove results, remove the cost objection, then make the ask trivially easy.

figures.caption: The hero leads with recovered results and a phone number in the header, so the highest-intent visitors can act without scrolling.
figures.alt: Dark hero section with a group photo of attorneys, a bold recovered-for-clients headline, a phone number in the top bar, and a yellow free case evaluation button.

figures.caption: Result cards pair the final award with the pre-trial offer, turning an abstract claim about never settling into inspectable evidence.
figures.alt: Navy section titled We Never Settle for Less with two white case cards showing car accident verdicts against much smaller pre-trial offers, beside an attorney portrait.

figures.caption: A quiet values section states who the firm fights for in plain language, giving hesitant visitors a reason to believe before the ask.
figures.alt: Light section titled We Fight For The People with short paragraphs of plain-language copy beside a photo of a gavel resting on a book and cash.

figures.caption: A side-by-side table contrasts retainer and contingency billing, dismantling the cost objection right before the evaluation CTA.
figures.alt: Light comparison section titled It's Free Unless We Win with two columns comparing retainer-based and contingency-based models above a yellow CTA button.

figures.caption: The evaluation form asks only what intake needs, with a lawyer-and-client photo alongside to keep the step feeling human, not legal.
figures.alt: Light section with a photo of a lawyer speaking with an older client next to a short case evaluation form with name, contact, zip code, case type, and description fields.

validation.honest_line: Moderated sessions with first-time visitors showed the page communicates credibility and a clear next step, but a concept test cannot prove real claimants under real stress would convert.

appendix.framing: The system underneath the page: a trust-first palette, a heavy Poppins type scale, and a button set built around one unmistakable yellow action.

figures.caption: Deep blue carries authority, icy blue softens it, and a single loud yellow is reserved for the actions that matter.
figures.alt: Primary color swatches on a dark board: Sonic Blue, pale Icy Landscape, and bright yellow Pac-Man with hex values.

figures.caption: Button states from filled yellow to ghost and icon-only keep one action color while giving secondary paths quieter forms.
figures.alt: Button component sheet showing yellow filled, outlined, text-only, and circular icon buttons in default and disabled states on a dark background.
